verses.verse:
तस्य क्रमस्य निर्वाहो यदा सर्वत्र क्रीयते।
समात्रिक समूहेषु तदाऽलंकार कल्पना।१११।
verses.text: When that order is carried through everywhere, in groups of equal mātrās (beats), then [there is] the making of an alaṅkāra (patterned exercise).

commentary.text: That is, if the order stated before is carried through, step by step, in the following notes, and those mātrās (beats) are also kept in mind, the alaṅkāra (patterned exercise) extends into a full ascending and descending form.

The point is that in the sādhanā (practice) of alaṅkāra one has to keep two kinds of order in mind - one is the order which you have made in two or three notes; the other is the general order of ascent and descent, which is fixed by the śāstra according to the rāga or thāṭ (parent scale). Suppose you composed this order "Sa Re Ga Re Sa" in three notes, which is in five mātrās (beats). If you carry this same order through Re Ga Ma in place of Sa Re Ga, then in place of Sa there will be Re, in place of Re Ga, and in place of Ga Ma, and the second link has formed like this: Re Ga Ma Ga Re. In the same way keep shifting each note forward until it ends on the Ṡa of the tāra saptaka (upper octave). Then, to come back from there, the same order has to be changed into its descending state. That is, the place that Re has in the ascent, Ni will have that same place in the descent. In this way the descending form of Sa Re Ga Re Sa will be Ṡa Ni Dha Ni Ṡa. Now if we want to play its full extension, we should first write it out as below and then play it. Doing so, we can gain an easy flow even in difficult alaṅkāras.

commentary.text: (The instruction is that) while writing, we went on writing the successive notes one below another, under each note, and while reading, went on reading from left to right. In this way both orders were carried through. To confirm the above, some alaṅkāras (patterned exercises) are being written. In these alaṅkāras, along with various elements and tālas (metric cycles), care has also been taken that they be practical. In these alaṅkāras some blank spaces are left for the sādhakas (practitioners). Fill them in and practise.

commentary.text: In the same way, in four notes too, other alaṅkāras (patterned exercises) can be composed in the form of a sūtra (formula) and spread across all the notes. For example - SaRe SaRe Sa Ga Re Ga SaRe SaRe SaMa SaMa GaMa| Sa ReRe SaRe GaGa Re Ga Sa Re Re Sa Re MaMa GaMa| Sa ReSa -Sa Re Sa GaGa Re Ga Sa ReSa Sa Re Sa MaMa GaMa, and so on.
